description: MOAS-23 (B-001): machine-readable golden-flow registry. Every flow ID below is explicit pass/fail/not-implemented when scripts/run-golden-flows.mjs runs — none are silently omitted. 'implemented' flows point to a real script under scripts/ that exercises the flow live against the running stack and asserts field-level outcomes (see each script for its specific assertions).

flows.description: Register near-duplicate and genuinely-distinct patients; verify fuzzy duplicate recall and zero false-block.
Canonical patient AI context surfaces active allergies; medication safety cross-reactivity check fires correctly.
Prescribe a brand-name drug that interacts with an existing prescription; verify the hard-stop fires by ingredient identity, not string match, and uncoded medicines surface a review flag.
Retrieve clinical guidelines by coded diagnosis when free-text synonyms are unmapped.
Create a medical-aid claim from a coded patient problem; verify SNOMED->ICD-10 auto-mapping and unmapped-concept surfacing.
Two differently-phrased encounters sharing one coded diagnosis aggregate as a single top-diagnoses row.
Create/read/update/search round trip for Patient, Encounter, Condition, AllergyIntolerance, Observation, MedicationRequest via the real FHIR API.
ServiceRequest/DiagnosticReport/DocumentReference create+read, and ImagingStudy search/read against real seeded DICOM study data.
FHIR Location/Organization return real tenant data; CapabilityStatement reconciles with controller-implemented interactions.
Live authenticated cross-role check: pharmacist/radiologist/receptionist/lab_tech correctly blocked from finance/billing/claims; accounts/admin correctly allowed.
Liveness independent of dependencies; readiness correctly reflects a real, injected database outage and recovery; six-probe smoke gate.
CDSS pytest suite collects and runs with pinned dependencies and no manual PYTHONPATH.
50-case AI evaluation harness with subgroup summaries, per-case artifacts, and reproducible parallel runs.
Backup->simulated data loss->restore->checksum verification on isolated synthetic tenant databases, with tenant-separation proof.

Drift/manual-triggered FL round -> real per-tenant sklearn training -> real weighted-ensemble global model aggregation -> leak-free holdout evaluation -> governed shadow staging, for deterioration/readmission/no_show/sepsis; also asserts admin-only access.
Real ICD-10-CM/SNOMED CT/SNOMED-to-ICD10 data volume, pattern validity, and referential integrity checks against the master DB (gap A-015/A-025 resolution).

Stated-vs-inferred relationship distinction, version/effective-time awareness, ECL query support, and FHIR Terminology Service (lookup/validate-code/subsumes/expand) operations, all against real loaded SNOMED/ICD-10 data.

flows.reason: Requires a live Daily.co API key and a WebRTC session to genuinely assert connection quality, not just room-creation HTTP status; MOAS-06 already fixed and live-verified room creation itself, but a full clinician<->patient session join is out of this harness's scripted-API scope.

MOAS-07 verified the escalation-event and duplicate-message-guard logic directly against a manually-published post-visit session (publish gate is blocked by an unrelated broken Whisper pipeline, per Sprint 1 notes) — a fully organic record->publish->follow-up journey is not yet scriptable end-to-end without that pipeline working.

Requires live LLM provider credentials for a genuine grounded-answer conversation; the underlying safety logic (duplicate-submission guard, deceased-patient suppression) was verified directly in Sprint 1/MOAS-07, but a full chat-turn journey needs a configured LLM backend not available in this sandboxed environment.

The imaging-order AI review pipeline requires an uploaded DICOM file and a configured vision-AI backend; this harness proved the FHIR ImagingStudy read path against seeded metadata (see radiography-imaging-study-roundtrip) but not the full upload->AI-review->radiologist-signoff journey.
Storeroom/inventory deduction on dispense was not exercised by this sprint's work; needs a dedicated flow asserting stock-level deltas, out of this session's remaining scope.

Sprint 5/MOAS-20 fixed and live-verified the RBAC boundary for payment-reconciliation endpoints; a full bank-statement-import->auto-match->reconciled-report journey with realistic bank-statement fixture data is separate, larger scope.
Requires the Zimbabwe HIV testing algorithm's multi-test sequential decision tree exercised with a realistic multi-visit fixture; not built this session.

Appointment/Encounter creation is exercised as a unit inside fhir-clinical-core-roundtrip (Encounter resource); a full scheduling-conflict/reschedule/no-show journey is broader scope not built this session.
Lab-result Observation create/read is covered by fhir-clinical-core-roundtrip; the full order->specimen-collection->result->clinician-review journey is broader scope not built this session.
Immunization FHIR resource mapping exists (MOAS-13/14 scope) but a catch-up-schedule clinical-logic journey was not built or tested this session.
Requires a second provisioned tenant to prove cross-facility referral continuity; this environment has only the single e2e-clinic tenant.

Patient-portal auth uses a separate PatientJwtAuthGuard flow (confirmed to exist and correctly scoped during MOAS-15's Location/Organization work) but a full self-registration->email-verification->login journey was not scripted this session.
PatientConsentService exists and is referenced by fhir.service.ts, but a dedicated consent-capture->enforcement-on-a-restricted-record journey was not built or tested this session.

MOAS-20 fixed and live-verified the RBAC boundary for the whole claims controller; a full submit->payer-response->remittance-import journey needs the medical-aid-demo-service's simulator wired in, which is explicitly documented (gap B-008) as a demo simulator, not a certified sandbox — a golden-flow claim here would be testing the demo simulator, not real payer behavior.

hipaa-audit.controller.ts's endpoints are correctly RBAC-gated (confirmed unaffected by MOAS-20's scan — already had @Roles()), but a full journey asserting a specific PHI access event appears correctly in the audit/breach-detection report was not built this session.
Requires a physical/simulator device exercising offline queueing and conflict resolution — explicitly out of this harness's server-API scope (see gap B-007).

resilience-backup-restore-integrity proves the backup/restore mechanism on synthetic data; a full multi-service failover/DR drill against production-like infrastructure is explicitly out of scope per MOAS-21's own stated boundary.
